news.title: Gianni Infantino is 'destroying the very essence' of football after World Cup plan
news.lede: Gianni Infantino is the victim of a smear campaign to boot him out of football, according to FIFA. The sport’s world governing body has blasted a ‘concerted and ongoing effort’ to ‘undermine’ both it and its president. It comes after it was claimed UEFA had to pay off Infantino’s former lover when he worked for the European football association. Infantino, 56, who worked for UEFA for 16 years before being elected FIFA president in 2016, has vehemently denied the allegation.

news.title: Infantino’s era is over, says La Liga boss as pressure mounts on Fifa
news.lede: Associations such as Uefa and the Football Association have called for Gianni Infantino to resign as Fifa president. (EPA Images pic) LONDON: La Liga president Javier Tebas claims Gianni Infantino is “destroying the very essence” of football and believes his time as Fifa president has come to an end, PA Media/dpa reported. Infantino has faced criticism following his failed plan to seek private investment in a company which would run Fifa’s competitions and sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. Fifa then revealed it “will not proceed” with plans, and Infantino on Wednesday apologised to national associations over how the plan was developed.

news.title: How Trabzonspor shocked Turkish rivals to make Mohamed Salah their Black Sea saviour
news.lede: Never before has a big name rejected Istanbul for Trabzon, but former Liverpool striker was offered more than riches. It began with a text sent during the World Cup. Ertugrul Dogan, the president of Trabzonspor, was watching Egypt when he picked up his phone and messaged his manager, Fatih Tekke. “Do you want Mohamed Salah?”

news.title: Vilda: Morocco’s World Cup Qualification Is the Result of a Women’s Football Project
news.lede: Rabat - Morocco women’s national team coach Jorge Vilda has hailed the country’s long-term investment in women’s football after the Atlas Lionesses qualified for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. Morocco booked their place at the global tournament by reaching the semi-finals of the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), following a 2-1 victory over South Africa on Saturday in Rabat. Speaking at the post-match press conference, Vilda said World Cup qualification had been one of the team’s main objectives from the beginning of the competition, describing the achievement as the result of the development project implemented by the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF). He stressed that the qualification was not the product of chance, but rather the outcome of sustained work and planning aimed at developing women’s football in Morocco.

news.title: Morocco and Algeria qualify for 2027 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: Algeria earned a historic first-time qualification for the Fifa Women’s World Cup, while Morocco punched their ticket to the quadrennial showpiece for a second consecutive time, thanks to their quarter-final victories in the Women's Africa Cup of Nations on Saturday. The Fennecs erased the heartbreak of their Wafcon quarter-final exit against Ghana on penalties from 12 months ago by defeating Ivory Coast 2-1 at Moulay Rachid Stadium in Casablanca on Saturday. Second-half goals from Ines Khiri and Amira Ould Braham cancelled Ivory Coast’s early lead via Ines Konan to send Algeria to the final four of the continental competition for the first time, where they will face Malawi or Ghana on Wednesday in Rabat. All four Wafcon semi-finalists gain automatic qualification to next year’s World Cup in Brazil.

news.title: Maradona’s ‘Hand of God’ Ball to Be Auctioned | Iconic 1986 World Cup Ball Could Fetch $10 Million
news.lede: Diego Maradona’s legendary “Hand of God” match ball from the 1986 FIFA World Cup quarterfinal between Argentina and England is set to go under the hammer in the United States this month. Heritage Auctions is scheduled to auction the iconic football from August 21 to 23, with an opening bid of $2.5 million. The auction house reportedly expects the historic ball to fetch around $10 million or more. The ball has been authenticated through photo matching, including detailed analysis of video footage and still images from the famous Argentina-England clash.

news.title: Fouzi Lekjaa and the ‘World Cup 2030 Government’: From Pitch to Premiership
news.lede: This past July 25, Fouzi Lekjaa — Morocco's Minister Delegate for the Budget and, since 2014, president of the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (RMFF) — formally joined the Party of Authenticity and Modernity (PAM) , taking an immediate seat on its Political Bureau . PAM's national coordinator Fatima-Zahra El Mansouri announced the news during the party's National Council in Salé, ending weeks of speculation and instantly becoming one of the most consequential political stories of Morocco's pre-electoral season. It arrived seven weeks before the legislative elections of 23 September 2026, which PAM has openly declared its ambition to finish first. Le Monde captured the moment by describing Lekjaa as "putting on the suit of a prime-ministerial contender," and Moroccan outlets have floated the idea, however speculative, of a future "World Cup 2030 government" led by the FRMF chief.
